title: Distance between two points
description: Calculates the distance between two points in a coordinate plane.

title: Midpoint Formula
description: Finds the midpoint of a line segment joining two points.
note: The midpoint divides the line segment into two equal parts.

title: Section Formula
description: Finds the coordinates of a point dividing a line segment internally in the ratio m:n.

example.question: Find the point dividing (1,2) and (7,8) in the ratio 1:2.

title: Centroid of Triangle
description: Finds the centroid of a triangle using the coordinates of its vertices.
note: The centroid is the intersection point of the medians.

title: Area of Triangle
description: Calculates the area of a triangle using coordinates.

example.question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (0,0), (4,0), (0,3).

note: If the area is zero, the points are collinear.

title: Slope of a Line
description: Calculates the slope (gradient) of a line joining two points.

example.question: Find the slope of the line joining (2,1) and (6,9).

note: Vertical lines have an undefined slope.

title: Distance of a Point from a Line
description: Calculates the perpendicular distance from a point to a straight line.

variables.meaning: Constants in the line Ax + By + C = 0

example.question: Find the distance of point (2,3) from the line 3x + 4y - 10 = 0.

note: The line must be written in the form Ax + By + C = 0.

title: Equation of a Circle
description: Represents a circle with centre (h,k) and radius r.

example.question: Write the equation of a circle with centre (2,-1) and radius 5.

note: If the centre is at the origin, the equation becomes x² + y² = r².

title: Equation of a Sphere
description: Represents a sphere with centre (h,k,l) and radius r.

example.question: Write the equation of a sphere with centre (1,2,3) and radius 4.

note: If the centre is at the origin, the equation becomes x²+y²+z²=r².

title: Pair of Straight Lines
description: Conditions for determining the nature of two straight lines.

example.question: Determine the nature of the pair of lines using coefficient ratios.

note: Compare the ratios of coefficients to identify the relationship between the lines.

title: Condition for Intersecting Lines
description: If the ratios of coefficients of x and y are different, the two lines intersect at exactly one point.

example.question: When do two straight lines intersect?

note: Intersecting lines have a unique solution.

title: Condition for Coincident Lines
description: If all three ratios are equal, both equations represent the same line.

example.question: When do two lines coincide?
example.solution: When all three coefficient ratios are equal.

note: Coincident lines have infinitely many solutions.

title: Condition for Parallel Lines
description: If the ratios of x and y coefficients are equal but the constant ratios are different, the lines are parallel.
note: Parallel lines never intersect and have no solution.
